title: Custom Tools
markdown:
**What it is:** When a job needs a tool the Executive doesn't have, it builds one on the spot rather than telling you it can't. A tool it is likely to need again, it keeps — those are your **custom tools**.

**What it does:**

- **Does repetitive work in one go.** "Create a reminder for each of these renewals", "file every scan in this Drive folder", "check each of these people's open items" — instead of working through the list one step at a time, the Executive builds a small tool for the job and runs it once. It's faster, and cheaper in AI usage.
- **Keeps what works.** When a tool it built did the job and the job will come up again, the Executive keeps it and says so. Next time it reuses the tool instead of building it again.
- **Works in chat and in workflows.** A workflow step can use the same approach for a folder of hundreds of files, and can reuse a kept tool when the step already has every tool it needs.
- **Stays inside the usual limits.** A custom tool can only do what the conversation or workflow using it is already allowed to do: the same tools, the same checks on who it reaches, the same approvals for anything new, and every action in the Audit Log. Only your own conversations can keep a tool or run a kept one — not someone emailing the Executive, a teammate, or a scheduled run.

**How to use:**

1. Just ask for the job — the Executive decides when building a tool makes sense. You can also say "do that for all of them" or "keep that so you can do it again".
2. Ask "what tools have you built?" to hear what it has kept.
3. Open **Settings → Advanced → Custom tools** to see each one: what it does, which of your tools it uses, how it works, every version and its recent runs.
4. Use the switch to turn a tool off, or **Use this one** on an earlier version to go back to it.
5. See how much work was done this way on **Token usage**, under **Done in one go**.

**Tips:**

- A turned-off tool never runs, and stays off even if the Executive improves it later — only you turn it back on.
- An operator can switch the whole feature off with `CHAT_SCRIPTS=false` (chat), `WORKFLOW_STEP_SCRIPTS=false` (workflows) or `SAVED_TOOLS_ENABLED=false` (keeping tools).
